chapter: Billy Pierce Studio and New York tap
title: Staying at the Belvedere Hotel as teenagers without a guardian
summary: Green and Chuckles stay at the Belvedere, aged fifteen and sixteen, not yet allowed to work on stage without a guardian.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you took a liking to Buddy Bradley and he took a liking to you, and that encouraged you to come up to his studio from Philadelphia?
Well, where did you stay when you were in New York?
The Belvedere Hotel. That's until Nat Nazarra and Buck and Bubbles came along.
Uh-huh. So you were staying along with Chuckles?
You two were staying alone at the hotel?
You were only how old at that time?

Well, we were teenagers, see. I was in my 15th year. Chuckles was 16. He was going into his 16th year. He was nine months older than I, and, as I was saying, we had the name of Shorty and Slim, you see.

See, but to work -- to work on the stage, we still weren't allowed to go on the stage unless we had guardian, you know, of some sort like that, and Mr. Robey, he was -- he was a fight you see promoter, and he wasn't actually in show business.
Well, were you working on the stage at this point?
At all? So you hadn't actually performed in front of an audience since the time when you were with the --

This charity show in Philadelphia at the Hippodrome Theater there at that time. They had one in Philadelphia, and they had one over here on Third Avenue in New York City, you see. And -- we were like aging, you see. Mr. Robey was supposed to come back like in -- and he would -- we were supposed to stay with him like until we became of age like, you see.
